mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy remains accommodative.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL monthly increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation, triggering Federal Reserve rate hikes that reduce equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous HOUST and RSAFS increases exceeding 0.5% indicate robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances with both HOUST and RSAFS rising > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE below 4.0% with declining trend signals late-cycle labor market overheating, prompting monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with UNRATE < 4.0% and falling.

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO above 100 reflects strong industrial production, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances with INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: HOUST decline exceeding 1.0% indicates weakening housing market demand, triggering short-term equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with HOUST fall > 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.2pp signal labor market tightening, leading to wage inflation and monetary policy shifts that cause negative S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with both PAYEMS rise > 0.5% and UNRATE fall > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS increase exceeding 0.5% over three months indicates active monetary tightening, raising discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% in 3 months.
